assignedReviews.card_evidence: Frogs jump far and fast mainly to escape predators like snakes and birds
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a behavioral response (jumping to escape) rather than an evolutionary change or adaptation such as mimicry or camouflage. It does not support the competency's focus on how animals have changed to better suit their environment.

copy.en:
Why do frogs jump so far?

Frogs jump far and fast mainly to escape predators like snakes and birds — one big leap can get them to safety before they're caught!
copy.tl:
Bakit malayo ang lukso ng palaka?

Lumulukso nang malayo at bigla ang palaka lalo na para makatakas sa mga kaaway tulad ng ahas at ibon — sa isang malakas na lukso, ligtas na agad ito!
copy.bis:
Nganong layo ang lukso sa baki?

Molukso og layo ug kalit ang baki labi na aron makaikyas sa mga kaaway sama sa bitin ug langgam — sa usa ka kusog nga lukso, luwas dayon kini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Toads usually make short little hops on the ground, while many true frogs leap much farther and higher.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes jumping behavior differences between toads and frogs but does not mention any outer body parts (head, legs, wings) or their role in movement or food gathering. It only touches on movement, not the anatomical structures the competency requires.

copy.en:
Do all frogs jump the same way?

Not quite! Toads usually make short little hops on the ground, while many true frogs leap much farther and higher.
copy.tl:
Pareho ba ang talon ng palaka at toad?

Hindi pareho! Karaniwang maiikli lang ang lukso ng toad sa lupa, habang mas malayo at mas mataas ang lukso ng maraming tunay na palaka.
copy.bis:
Managsama ba ang lukso sa baki ug toad?

Dili managsama! Kasagaran mubo ra ang lukso sa toad sa yuta, samtang mas layo ug mas taas ang lukso sa daghang tinuod nga baki.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The frontal lobe at the front of your brain! It handles decisions, planning, and behavior
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a function of the frontal lobe (a part of the nervous system) but does not use models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations, and does not explain how body systems work together (e.g., digestion and excretion). It only mentions a single brain function, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it doesn't fully develop until early adulthood
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions brain development, which is tangentially related to growth, but it does not describe the general characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). It focuses on a specific brain function rather than the broad concept of living things growing, responding, and reproducing.

copy.en:
What part of your brain makes decisions?

The frontal lobe at the front of your brain! It handles decisions, planning, and behavior — and it doesn't fully develop until early adulthood.
copy.tl:
Anong bahagi ng utak ang nagpapasya para sa'yo?

Ang frontal lobe sa harap ng utak! Ito ang namamahala sa paggawa ng desisyon, pagpaplano, at ugali — pero hindi pa ito ganap na umuunlad hanggang tayo'y lumaki.
copy.bis:
Unsang bahin sa utok ang nagdesisyon alang nimo?

Ang frontal lobe sa atubangan sa utok! Kini ang nag-atiman sa paghimo og desisyon, pagplano, ug ugali — apan wala pa kini hingpit matubo hangtod sa sayo nga pagkabatan-on.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Water vapor turns straight into tiny ice crystals on leaves and grass
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a gas-to-solid change (deposition) caused by temperature, but G5-M-6 focuses on temperature-driven changes such as solid to liquid to gas (melting, evaporation). The card does not teach the melting/evaporation processes named in the competency, only a different state change.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Water vapor turns straight into tiny ice crystals on leaves and grass
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: G6-M-1 requires describing changes of state (melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation) using diagrams and flowcharts. The card describes deposition (gas to solid) without using diagrams or flowcharts, and does not address the listed processes. It shares the topic of state changes but does not directly support this competency.

copy.en:
Have you ever seen frost on grass in the morning? How does it form?

Frost forms when a surface drops below 0°C! Water vapor turns straight into tiny ice crystals on leaves and grass — it skips being liquid dew entirely!
copy.tl:
Nakita mo na ba ang frost sa damo sa umaga? Paano ito nabubuo?

Nabubuo ang frost kapag lumamig ang ibabaw sa ibaba ng 0°C! Direktang nagiging maliliit na kristal ng yelo ang singaw ng tubig sa dahon at damo — hindi nagiging hamog!
copy.bis:
Nakita na ba nimo ang frost sa sagbot sa buntag? Unsaon pagporma niini?

Maporma ang frost kon ang patong molamig ubos sa 0°C! Ang singaw sa tubig diretso nga mahimong gagmay nga kristal sa yelo sa dahon ug sagbot — dili una mahimong yamog!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a fruit bat wraps its wings around its body
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions wings as an outer body part, but the role described (warmth and protection) is not the role specified in the competency (move and gather food).

assignedReviews.card_evidence: wraps its wings around its body like a cozy cloak to stay warm and protected
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a behavioral adaptation for warmth/protection, but the competency specifically asks for examples like mimicry or camouflage and requires use of secondary sources; the card does not directly support the stated skill.

copy.en: When resting, a fruit bat wraps its wings around its body like a cozy cloak to stay warm and protected.
copy.tl: Kapag natutulog, binabalot ng paniki ang mga pakpak nito sa katawan parang balabal para manatiling mainit at protektado.
copy.bis: Kon matulog, giputos sa kabog ang iyang mga pako libot sa lawas sama sa kupo aron magpabiling init ug panalipdan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The fruit dove has such a soft, cooing call

assignedReviews.card_evidence: soft, cooing call that people often hear it in the trees
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a sound (the bird's call) and that it is heard, but it does not explore or describe how sound is made or transferred. It merely states that the call is soft and heard, without any explanation of sound production or transmission, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: The fruit dove has such a soft, cooing call that people often hear it in the trees without ever spotting it.
copy.tl: Ang huni ng fruit dove ay napakahina at parang malambing na ungol, kaya madalas itong naririnig pero hindi nakikita.
copy.bis: Ang huni sa fruit dove hinay kaayo ug morag malumo nga ungol, mao nga kanunay kining madungog apan dili makita.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Faster in a warm place and more slowly in a cold refrigerator!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the factors affecting the rates of chemical reactions as applied in food preservation and materials production, control of fire, pollution, and corrosion

Ripening is not presented as a chemical reaction nor linked to these applications.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Faster in a warm place and more slowly in a cold refrigerator!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes in properties of materials when exposed to certain changes in temperature, such as changes when wood or coal are burned
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions temperature affecting fruit ripening, but the competency requires describing changes in properties of materials when exposed to temperature changes, with examples like burning wood or coal. Fruit ripening is not a material property change of the type intended, and no property change is described.

copy.en:
How do fruits like bananas ripen in warm and cold places?

Faster in a warm place and more slowly in a cold refrigerator!
copy.tl:
Paano nahihinog ang mga prutas tulad ng saging sa mainit at malamig na lugar?

Mas mabilis sa mainit na lugar at mas mabagal sa malamig na ref!
copy.bis:
Unsaon paghinog ang mga prutas sama sa saging sa init ug bugnaw nga dapit?

Mas paspas sa init nga dapit ug mas hinay sa bugnaw nga ref!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Fruits and vegetables are packed with vitamins and minerals that strengthen your body and keep you healthy!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the nutritional value of fruits and vegetables, which relates to food as a basic need, but it does not teach the concept of basic needs (air, food, water, shelter) or help students identify them. It is about healthy eating, not the fundamental needs of living things.

copy.en: Fruits and vegetables are packed with vitamins and minerals that strengthen your body and keep you healthy!
copy.tl: Ang mga prutas at gulay ay punong-puno ng bitamina at mineral na nagpapalakas ng katawan at tumutulong sa atin na manatiling malusog!
copy.bis: Ang mga prutas ug utanon puno sa bitamina ug mineral nga makapalig-on sa lawas ug makatabang kanato nga magpabiling himsog!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The original Fujita scale measures tornado strength from F0, which is weak, all the way to F5, the strongest!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe some effects of weather disturbances that occur in or near the Philippines
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the Fujita scale for tornado strength, which is a weather disturbance, but it does not describe any effects of weather disturbances in or near the Philippines. It only gives the range of the scale, not impacts or consequences.

copy.en: The original Fujita scale measures tornado strength from F0, which is weak, all the way to F5, the strongest!
copy.tl: Ang orihinal na Fujita scale ay sumusukat mula F0 na mahina, hanggang sa F5 na pinakamalakas!
copy.bis: Ang orihinal nga Fujita scale nagsukod gikan sa F0 nga huyang, hangtod sa F5 nga labing kusog!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A fungus digests its food outside its body first, then soaks it up through tiny thread-like hyphae that work like roots
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not use a table to classify living things into the named groups.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A fungus digests its food outside its body first, then soaks it up through tiny thread-like hyphae
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web
assignedReviews.reason: External digestion by hyphae is not the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web.

copy.en:
How does a fungus eat its food?

A fungus digests its food outside its body first, then soaks it up through tiny thread-like hyphae that work like roots.
copy.tl:
Paano kumakain ang fungi?

Tinutunaw muna ng fungi ang pagkain sa labas ng katawan nito, tapos sinisipsip ito gamit ang manipis na sinulid na hyphae na parang ugat.
copy.bis:
Giunsa pagkaon sa fungi ang iyang pagkaon?

Tunawon una sa fungi ang pagkaon sa gawas sa iyang lawas, dayon suyopon kini gamit ang nipis nga sinulid nga hyphae nga sama sa gamot.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Some mushrooms, like oyster mushrooms, are safe to eat
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses edible vs poisonous mushrooms, which touches on fungi, but it does not use a table to classify living things into the named groups (plants, animals, microorganisms) as required by the competency.

copy.en: Some mushrooms, like oyster mushrooms, are safe to eat — but some wild mushrooms are poisonous, so never eat one you don't recognize.
copy.tl: May mga kabuteng ligtas kainin tulad ng oyster mushroom, pero may mga ligaw na kabuteng nakakalason, kaya huwag kumain ng kabuteng hindi kilala.
copy.bis: Adunay mga uhong nga luwas kan-on sama sa oyster mushroom, apan adunay ihalas nga uhong nga makahilo, busa ayaw pagkaon og uhong nga wala mailhi.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Fungi can't make their own food, so they're called heterotrophs — they must get it from other living things
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not use a table to classify living things into the named groups.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they must get it from other living things
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web
assignedReviews.reason: Heterotrophs getting food from other living things is not the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web.

copy.en:
Why is fungi called a heterotroph?

Fungi can't make their own food, so they're called heterotrophs — they must get it from other living things.
copy.tl:
Bakit tinatawag na heterotroph ang fungi?

Hindi makagawa ng sariling pagkain ang fungi, kaya tinatawag itong heterotroph — kailangan nilang kumuha nito sa ibang buhay na bagay.
copy.bis:
Ngano gitawag og heterotroph ang fungi?

Dili makahimo og kaugalingong pagkaon ang fungi, mao nga gitawag kini og heterotroph — kinahanglan nila kining kuhaon gikan sa ubang buhi.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Black bread mold has two kinds of hyphae
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes hyphae of black bread mold, a fungus, but does not use a table or classify living things into the named groups. It only mentions a microorganism without supporting the classification skill required by the competency.

copy.en: Black bread mold has two kinds of hyphae: some poke down to soak up food, and others stand up with tiny black balls at the tip holding spores — those are the black dots you see!
copy.tl: Ang itim na amag ng tinapay ay may dalawang klase ng hyphae: ang ilan ay tumutusok pababa para sumipsip ng pagkain, at ang iba ay tumataas na may maliliit na itim na bilog sa dulo na may spore — iyon ang mga itim na tuldok na nakikita mo!
copy.bis: Ang itom nga agup-op sa tinapay adunay duha ka klase sa hyphae: ang uban mutusok paubos aron mosuyop og pagkaon, ug ang uban motindog nga adunay gagmay nga itom nga lingin sa tumoy nga adunay spore — kana ang gagmay nga itom nga tuldok nga imong makita!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Many mushrooms appear, release their spores, and wither away -- all within just a few days.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions fungi (mushrooms) but does not use a table or classify living things into the named groups. assignedReviews.card_evidence: Many mushrooms appear, release their spores, and wither away -- all within just a few days.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes mushrooms appearing, releasing spores, and withering, which touches on reproduction and growth but does not explicitly describe the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce) as a general concept. It is a specific example without direct instructional support for the competency's skill of describing these characteristics.

copy.en: Many mushrooms appear, release their spores, and wither away -- all within just a few days.
copy.tl: Maraming kabute ang lumalabas, naglalabas ng spore, at nalalanta -- lahat sa loob lamang ng ilang araw.
copy.bis: Daghang uhong ang mogawas, mopagawas sa ilang spore, ug malaya -- tanan sulod lang sa pipila ka adlaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Unlike plants, fungi have no true roots, leaves, or seeds!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a distinguishing characteristic of fungi but does not use a table to classify living things into the named groups, as required by the competency. The format-required table is absent, so the card is at most related_only.

copy.en:
What don't fungi have?

Unlike plants, fungi have no true roots, leaves, or seeds!
copy.tl:
Ano ang wala sa fungi?

Hindi tulad ng halaman, walang tunay na ugat, dahon, o buto ang mga fungi!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang wala sa fungi?

Dili sama sa tanom, ang fungi walay tinuod nga gamot, dahon, o liso!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: common observable physical traits passed to offspring
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to explain how lines of evidence, such as fossils, biogeography, and comparative morphology, support the occurrence of evolution
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes physical traits (fur, body shape, number of legs) passed to offspring, which is about inheritance of traits, not about lines of evidence (fossils, biogeography, comparative morphology) supporting evolution. It does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: Like dogs, cats, and goats, common observable physical traits passed to offspring are the presence of fur, body shape, and number of legs.
copy.tl: Tulad ng aso, pusa, at kambing, ang mga karaniwang nakikitang pisikal na katangian na ipinapasa sa mga anak ay ang pagkakaroon ng balahibo, hugis ng katawan, at bilang ng mga binti.
copy.bis: Sama sa iro, iring, ug kanding, ang kasagarang makita nga pisikal nga mga kinaiya nga gipasa sa mga liwat mao ang presensya sa balahibo, porma sa lawas, ug gidaghanon sa mga tiil.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Small colored plastic fuses protect the lights, wipers, and radio.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that electricity is a flow of electrons and show appreciation for the need to observe safe measures in handling electricity
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes fuses in cars as protective devices and mentions replacing a blown fuse, but it does not teach that electricity is a flow of electrons nor does it explain safe measures for handling electricity. It shares the broad topic of electrical safety but provides no direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: Cars have fuse boxes too! Small colored plastic fuses protect the lights, wipers, and radio. If they suddenly stop working, a fuse probably blew and needs replacing!
copy.tl: May fuse box din ang mga kotse! Pinoprotektahan ng maliliit na kulay-kulay na plastic fuse ang ilaw, wiper, at radyo. Kung biglang ayaw gumana, baka may natunaw na fuse!
copy.bis: Aduna pud fuse box ang mga kotse! Giprotektahan sa gagmay nga kolorado nga plastic fuse ang suga, wiper, ug radyo. Kung kalit dili mogana, basin adunay natunaw nga fuse!

assignedReviews.reason: The card gives an example of a chemical change (adobo cooking) and mentions a reaction altering chemical structure, but it does not explain that bond formation/breaking constitutes a chemical change or that a new substance forms. assignedReviews.card_evidence: Cooking chicken adobo involves a chemical change because the acetic acid in vinegar reacts with the meat proteins to alter their chemical structure and flavor!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain why physical changes are reversible, and chemical changes are irreversible
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies cooking adobo as a chemical change but does not address reversibility/irreversibility of physical vs. chemical changes, which is the core of the competency. It provides no contrast with physical changes or explanation of irreversibility.

copy.en: Cooking chicken adobo involves a chemical change because the acetic acid in vinegar reacts with the meat proteins to alter their chemical structure and flavor!
copy.tl: Ang pagluluto ng chicken adobo ay isang chemical change dahil ang acetic acid sa suka ay nakikipag-reaksyon sa mga protina ng karne para baguhin ang kanilang chemical structure at lasa!
copy.bis: Ang pagluto sa chicken adobo kay usa ka chemical change kay ang acetic acid sa suka mo-react sa mga protina sa karne aron usbon ang ilang chemical structure ug lami!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: air resistance, which is scientifically classified as a type of fluid friction
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how friction can produce heat and investigate ways of reducing and increasing friction
assignedReviews.reason: The card only classifies air resistance as a type of fluid friction. It does not demonstrate how friction produces heat or investigate ways of reducing and increasing friction, which are the actions in the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A skydiver falling through the atmosphere experiences air resistance
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to demonstrate that pushes and pulls can be used to change the speed and direction of an object including making it go faster, turn it to a different direction, slow it down, and stop it
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a falling skydiver, which involves motion, but it does not demonstrate that pushes and pulls can change speed or direction, nor does it address making objects go faster, turn, slow down, or stop. The content is only tangentially related to forces and movement.

copy.en: A skydiver falling through the atmosphere experiences air resistance, which is scientifically classified as a type of fluid friction!
copy.tl: Ang isang skydiver na bumabagsak sa atmosphere ay nakararanas ng air resistance, na siyentipikong naka-classify bilang isang uri ng fluid friction!
copy.bis: Ang skydiver nga nahulog sa atmosphere nakasinati og air resistance, nga sa science gi-classify isip usa ka klase sa fluid friction!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Microscopic water bears called tardigrades can survive the freezing vacuum of outer space for several days!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an extreme survival ability of tardigrades but does not describe how they have changed (evolved/adapted) to better suit their environment, which is the core of G5-L-9. It lacks any mention of adaptation, change, or evolutionary process, so it only shares the broad topic of animals and environments.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Microscopic water bears called tardigrades can survive the freezing vacuum of outer space for several days!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions survival in extreme conditions but does not describe the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). It does not directly support any of these three characteristics, so it is only tangentially related to living things.

copy.en:
What tiny animal can survive outer space?

Microscopic water bears called tardigrades can survive the freezing vacuum of outer space for several days!
copy.tl:
Anong maliit na hayop ang nabubuhay sa outer space?

Ang maliliit na hayop na tinatawag na tardigrades o water bears ay kayang mabuhay sa nagyeyelong vacuum ng outer space ng ilang araw!
copy.bis:
Unsang gamay nga hayop ang mabuhi sa outer space?

Ang microscopic nga hayop nga gitawag ug tardigrades o water bears makasurvive sa nagyeyelong vacuum sa outer space sulod sa pipila ka adlaw!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sweat and dark clothing attract bees!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses bee behavior and safety tips (avoiding stings) but does not describe the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). It only mentions bees as living things without teaching the competency's concept.

copy.en: Sweat and dark clothing attract bees! Shower before going outside and wear light colors to lower your chance of getting stung.
copy.tl: Ang pawis at madidilim na damit ay nakakaakit ng bubuyog! Mag-shower ka bago lumabas at magsuot ng magagaan na kulay para di ka makagat.
copy.bis: Ang singot ug itom nga sinina makadani sa mga putyukan! Mag-shower una mogawas ug magsul-ob og hayag nga kolor aron malikayan ang samad.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they would stretch about 160,000 kilometers
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the circulatory system as heart, blood, and blood vessels, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: Total vessel length is trivia, not identifying heart, blood, and blood vessels and how they work.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: If you laid out all the blood vessels in an adult body end-to-end
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: Vessel-length trivia is not the five body systems as a set.

copy.en:
How long are all your blood vessels?

If you laid out all the blood vessels in an adult body end-to-end, they would stretch about 160,000 kilometers!
copy.tl:
Gaano kahaba ang lahat ng daluyan ng dugo mo?

Kung ilalatag ang lahat ng daluyan ng dugo ng isang matanda nang sunud-sunod, aabot ito sa humigit-kumulang 160,000 kilometro!
copy.bis:
Unsa kataas ang tanan mong blood vessels?

Kung ihan-ay ang tanang blood vessels sa usa ka adulto nga sunod-sunod, moabot kini og mga 160,000 kilometro!

Why shouldn't you use water on a grease fire?

Oil is less dense than water, so it floats! That's why you must never use water to extinguish a grease fire.

Mas magaan ang oil kaysa tubig kaya lumulutang ito. Kaya bawal ang tubig sa grease fire!

Nganong dili magamit ang tubig sa grease fire?

Mas magaan ang oil kaysa tubig, mao nga molutaw kini. Dili pwede ang tubig sa grease fire!

Leaving it at room temperature lets bacteria multiply rapidly!
copy.tl:
Bakit dapat agad ilagay sa ref ang hindi natapos na kanin?

Kapag iniwan sa labas, mabilis na dumadami ang bakterya!
copy.bis:
Nganong dapat dayon ibutang sa ref ang dili na makakaon nga kan-on?

Kung pasagdan sa gawas, dali ra kaayo mudaghan ang bakterya!

How much energy does your brain use every day?

Your brain uses about 20 percent of your body's total energy! It consumes roughly 300 kilocalories daily just to process thoughts and signals.

Gaano karaming energy ang ginagamit ng utak mo araw-araw?

Ang utak mo ay gumagamit ng halos 20 percent ng total energy ng katawan! Kumakain ito ng mga 300 kilocalories araw-araw para mag-process ng thoughts at signals.
copy.bis:
Unsa kadaghan nga enerhiya ang gigamit sa imong utok kada adlaw?

Ang imong utok mogamit ug mga 20 percent sa total nga enerhiya sa lawas! Nag-consume kini ug mga 300 kilocalories kada adlaw para mag-process sa thoughts ug signals.

copy.bis: Ang Philippine carabao nagkaon og sagbot aron makuha ang chemical energy! Iyang lawas i-convert kini ngadto sa kinetic energy para mag-uma.

copy.tl: Ang parachute ay gumagamit ng air friction, na tinatawag ding drag, para pabagalin ang paghulog ng skydiver hanggang sa ligtas na bilis!
copy.bis: Ang parachute mogamit og air friction, nga gitawag pud og drag, aron hinay-hinayon ang paghulog sa skydiver hangtod sa luwas nga landing speed!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: plan and carry out a scientific investigation to determine the effect of different surfaces on the size of frictional forces

How does friction help you walk forward?

Friction between your rubber shoes and the ground pushes you forward when you walk instead of only slowing objects down.
copy.tl:
Paano ka tinutulak ng friction pasulong kapag naglalakad?

Ang friction o pagkapit ng goma ng sapatos mo sa lupa ang nagtutulak sa'yo pasulong kapag naglalakad, hindi lang ito nagpapabagal.
copy.bis:
Giunsa ka sa friction nga mapasulod kung maglakaw?

Ang friction o pagkupot sa goma sa sapatos nimo sa yuta mao ang nag-push nimo padulong sa unahan kung maglakaw ka, dili lang kini mag-hinay-hinay.

How much space does steam take up compared to liquid water?

When liquid water boils into steam, one milliliter expands to fill about 1,700 milliliters of space as a gas!

Gaano kalaki ang espasyong kinakapit ng steam kumpara sa likidong tubig?

Kapag kumukulo ang likidong tubig at nagiging steam, ang isang milliliter ay lumalawak at sumasakop ng halos 1,700 milliliters bilang gas!
copy.bis:
Unsa kadako nga space ang gipanag-iya sa steam kumpara sa liquid water?

Kung mo-boil ang liquid water ngadto sa steam, ang usa ka milliliter mo-expand aron mapuno ang mga 1,700 milliliters isip gas!

Anaerobic bacteria break down the manure inside sealed biodigesters to produce methane gas for cooking!

Paano tayo nakakakuha ng cooking gas mula sa dumi ng kalabaw?

Ang anaerobic bacteria ay nagbubungkag nito sa loob ng sealed biodigesters para makagawa ng methane gas para sa pagluluto!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagkuha og cooking gas gikan sa abono sa kalabaw?

Ang anaerobic bacteria nagbungkag niini sa sulod sa sealed biodigesters aron makaproduce og methane gas nga gigamit sa pagluto!

Do goldfish really forget in seconds?

Not true! Goldfish actually remember things for months — they even recognize feeding times and their human owners.
copy.tl:
Talaga bang segundo lang matandaan ng goldfish?

Hindi totoo! Ang goldfish pala ay may memoryang tumatagal ng ilang buwan — natatandaan nila ang oras ng pagpapakain at kilala pa nila ang kanilang mga tao.
copy.bis:
Segundos ra ba gyud mahinumdom ang goldfish?

Dili tinuod! Ang goldfish diay adunay memorya nga molungtad og mga buwan — mahinumduman nila ang oras sa pagpakaon ug mailhan pa nila ang ilang mga tag-iya.

Kung 100 pounds ang timbang mo sa Earth, mga 16.5 pounds lang ang timbang mo sa Moon!
copy.bis:

Kung 100 pounds ang gibug-aton nimo sa Earth, mga 16.5 pounds ra ang gibug-aton nimo sa Moon!

Sinisira ng sabon ang mataba (lipid) na balot ng mga virus, kaya napipigilan ang pagkalat ng impeksyon!

Nganong epektibo ang paghugas sa kamot gamit ang sabon?

Gigub-on sa sabon ang tambok nga panit sa mga virus, mao nga mapugngan ang pagkatap sa impeksyon!

Kayang sumipsip ng tubig ang napakalaking dami ng heat energy nang hindi agad tumataas ang temperatura, kaya nakakatulong ito sa pag-regulate ng klima!

Unsaon pag-regulate sa tubig sa klima sa mga baybayon?

Makasuyop ang tubig ug daghang heat energy nga dili dali mosaka ang temperatura, maong makatabang kini sa pag-regulate sa klima sa mga baybayon!

Helium gas is lighter than air, allowing one cubic meter to lift roughly one kilogram of weight!

Mas magaan kaysa hangin ang helium gas, kaya isang cubic meter nito ay kayang buhatin ang isang kilo ng bigat!
copy.bis:
Pila ka kilo ang kayang i-lift sa usa ka cubic meter sa helium gas?

Mas gaan kaysa hangin ang helium gas, mao nga usa ka cubic meter makapabug-at og mga usa ka kilo!

At room temperature, honey is about 10,000 times more viscous than water, making it super thick and slow!
copy.tl:

Sa temperatura ng silid, ang pulot ay mga 10,000 beses na mas malapot kaysa tubig, kaya napakabagal niya!

Nganong mas hinay mo-agos ang likidong honey kaysa sa tubig?

Sa temperatura sa kwarto, ang honey mga 10,000 ka beses nga mas lapot kaysa tubig, mao nga hinay kaayo kini!

Over one trillion! Scientists discovered the human nose can detect and remember more than a trillion different scents.

Higit sa isang trilyon! Natuklasan ng mga siyentipiko na kaya ng ilong ng tao na amuyin at alalahanin ang higit sa isang trilyong iba't ibang amoy.

It does not explain how earthquakes result in tsunamis, nor does it mention earthquakes, shoreline communities, or the mechanism of devastation. It shares the topic of tsunamis but provides no instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: The 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami was one of the deadliest natural disasters in recorded history.
copy.tl: Ang 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami ay isa sa pinakamapanganib na natural disasters sa nakatalang kasaysayan.
copy.bis: Ang 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami usa sa pinakamatay nga natural disasters sa narekord nga kasaysayan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sensory nerves send a signal to your spinal cord, which instantly triggers motor nerves to pull your hand away from the heat.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains a specific reflex mechanism (sensory nerves, spinal cord, motor nerves) but does not describe the general characteristic that living things respond. It is an advanced nervous-system example, not a grade-3 lesson on the characteristics of living things. It shares the concept of 'response' only tangentially.

copy.en:
Why do you yank your hand away from something hot?

Sensory nerves send a signal to your spinal cord, which instantly triggers motor nerves to pull your hand away from the heat.
copy.tl:
Bakit bigla mong nahihila ang kamay mo sa init?

Ang sensory nerves ay nagpapadala ng signal sa spinal cord, na agad na nag-uutos sa motor nerves para hilahin ang kamay mo palayo sa init.
copy.bis:
Nganong kalit mong mabira ang imong kamot sa init?

Ang sensory nerves nagpadala og signal sa spinal cord, nga dayon nagsugo sa motor nerves aron ibira ang imong kamot palayo sa kainit.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Pacific Ocean covers about 32 percent of Earth's surface area
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify what proportion of the Earth's surface is covered with water as opposed to land
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives the Pacific Ocean's share of Earth's surface, not the total proportion of water versus land. It does not directly teach the overall water/land coverage ratio required by the competency.

copy.en: The Pacific Ocean covers about 32 percent of Earth's surface area, making it larger than all landmasses combined!
copy.tl: Ang Pacific Ocean ay sumasakop ng halos 32 porsyento ng surface area ng Earth, kaya mas malaki ito kaysa lahat ng lupain na pinagsama!
copy.bis: Ang Pacific Ocean nagtabon ug mga 32 porsyento sa surface area sa kalibutan, mas dako pa ni kaysa tanang yuta nga nag-uban!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it sinks and instantly vaporizes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions vaporization but does not describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases, and does not use diagrams or flowcharts as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it sinks and instantly vaporizes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card only mentions water vaporizing in a fire-safety context; it does not describe how temperature changes cause matter to change state generally, such as solid to liquid to gas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Water is denser than oil, so it sinks and instantly vaporizes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes in properties of materials when exposed to certain changes in temperature, such as changes when wood or coal are burned
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about oil fire safety and water density/vaporization, not about changes in properties of materials when exposed to temperature changes such as burning wood or coal.

copy.en:
Why is pouring water on burning oil so dangerous?

Water is denser than oil, so it sinks and instantly vaporizes, spreading the fire everywhere!
copy.tl:
Bakit delikado ang pagbuhos ng tubig sa nasusunog na mantika?

Mas mabigat ang tubig kaysa mantika, kaya lumulubog ito at agad na nag-evaporate, na nagkakalat ng apoy!
copy.bis:
Ngano delikado ang pagbubo og tubig sa nagdilaab nga mantika?

Mas bug-at ang tubig kaysa mantika, mao nga molubog kini ug dali ra mo-evaporate, nga mopakalat sa kalayo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: keratin, a strong solid protein material
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a solid material (keratin) and a property (strong), but it does not teach how to describe physical properties of solid materials in general, nor does it provide the kind of comparative or sensory properties (hard, shiny, stretchable) the competency targets. It is a single fact about eagle feathers, not instructional support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: keratin, a strong solid protein material
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify objects at home and in the classroom as solid, liquid or gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies keratin as a solid, but the competency requires identifying objects at home and in the classroom as solid, liquid, or gas. Eagle feathers and keratin are not typical home/classroom objects, and the card does not help students classify everyday objects into states of matter.

copy.en: The feathers of a Philippine Eagle are made of keratin, a strong solid protein material!
copy.tl: Ang mga balahibo ng Philippine Eagle ay gawa sa keratin, isang matibay na solid protein material!
copy.bis: Ang mga balahibo sa Philippine Eagle gihimo sa keratin, usa ka lig-on nga solid protein material!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Shaving a block of ice into fine flakes for your bowl of halo-halo is a perfect example of a physical change.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain why physical changes are reversible, and chemical changes are irreversible
assignedReviews.reason: The card only identifies shaving ice as an example of a physical change. It does not explain why physical changes are reversible or why chemical changes are irreversible, which is the core action of the competency.

copy.en:
Is shaving ice for halo-halo a physical change?

Yes! Shaving a block of ice into fine flakes for your bowl of halo-halo is a perfect example of a physical change.
copy.tl:
Pisikal ba ang pagbabago kapag kinakayod ang yelo para sa halo-halo?

Oo! Ang pag-shave ng block of ice into fine flakes para sa iyong bowl ng halo-halo ay isang halimbawa ng physical change.
copy.bis:
Physical change ba ang pagkayod sa yelo para sa halo-halo?

Oo! Ang pag-shave sa block of ice into fine flakes para sa imong bowl sa halo-halo kay pananglitan sa physical change.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: physical weathering
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain why physical changes are reversible, and chemical changes are irreversible
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions physical weathering, a physical change, but does not address reversibility of physical changes or irreversibility of chemical changes, which is the core of the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: physical weathering
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how soil is formed from rocks and minerals
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions weathering of limestone but does not explain how soil is formed from rocks and minerals. It only states that weathering occurs, without connecting it to soil formation.

copy.en: The solid limestone formations of the Chocolate Hills in Bohol slowly undergo physical weathering over time!
copy.tl: Ang solidong limestone formations ng Chocolate Hills sa Bohol ay dadaan sa physical weathering habang lumilipas ang panahon!
copy.bis: Ang solidong limestone formations sa Chocolate Hills sa Bohol moagi og physical weathering samtang nag‑labay ang panahon!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card only describes Earth's orbital motion due to gravity; it does not describe the general structure of the solar system, name major celestial objects, or address their features and composition.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Solar gravity pulls Earth inward, but its forward motion keeps our planet moving in a curved orbit!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a Sun-Earth-Moon system model to demonstrate and explain the observable effects of predictable patterns and events including changes in seasons, changes observed in the patterns of visible star over a year, and solar and lunar eclipses
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the Sun and Earth but does not involve a Sun-Earth-Moon model, the Moon, seasons, star patterns, or eclipses, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: Solar gravity pulls Earth inward, but its forward motion keeps our planet moving in a curved orbit!
copy.tl: Hinila ng gravity ng araw ang Earth papasok, pero ang pag-usad nito ang nagpapabilin sa planeta sa paikot na orbit!
copy.bis: Gihulbot sa gravity sa adlaw ang Earth pa-sulod, apan ang pag-usad niini nagpadayon sa planeta sa kurbado nga orbit!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: This hard mineral resists weathering much better than softer rocks.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore the school grounds or the local area to observe or collect different types of rocks, describing their similarities and differences in terms of features, such as texture, color, and grain crystal size
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions quartz as a hard mineral and its resistance to weathering, which is related to rocks and minerals, but it does not support the competency's focus on exploring, observing, or collecting different types of rocks and describing similarities/differences in texture, color, or grain crystal size.

copy.en:
What makes Boracay's white sand so special?

Boracay's white sand has tiny pieces of quartz! This hard mineral resists weathering much better than softer rocks.
copy.tl:
Ano ang nasa puting buhangin ng Boracay Beach?

Ang puting buhangin sa Boracay Beach ay may maliliit na piraso ng quartz—isang matigas na mineral na hindi madaling masira kumpara sa malalambot na bato!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang sulod sa puti nga balas sa Boracay Beach?

Ang puti nga balas sa Boracay Beach adunay gagmay nga piraso sa quartz—usa ka hard mineral nga dili dali ma-weather kumpara sa humok nga bato!
